To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vocabulary knowledge declines in amount and changes in structure beginning in mid-adulthood.

(1) the amount of word knowledge declines in healthy adults around the age of 65, (2) the structure of word knowledge becomes more differentiated in adults over 65, and (3) the two types of change may be causally related.
the amount of vocabulary knowledge declines beginning at about 65 years, and that the structure of vocabulary knowledge undergoes a shift in organization at about the same time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and development of vocabulary knowledge in adults.
the nature of age-related changes in the quantity and structure of vocabulary knowledge in adulthood.
the development of knowledge about word meanings in adulthood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantity and quality of vocabulary knowledge are both affected by the aging process, but the quality of knowledge is less affected than the quantity.
the quantity of word-knowledge declines across adulthood, and that the organization and structure of knowledge undergo qualitative changes after about 65.
vocabulary declines in both quantity and structure in the later years of adulthood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantity and structure of vocabulary knowledge change with age in adulthood.
vocabulary knowledge is a complex construct with a number of components.
there are both quantitative and qualitative changes in vocabulary knowledge in older age, and that the quantitative changes begin earlier than the qualitative changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for more research into age differences in the structure and organization of knowledge, especially in older adults.
the structure of vocabulary knowledge is relatively stable across adulthood, but that the amount of knowledge declines with age.
the study of vocabulary knowledge in adulthood needs to take into account the possibility that there may be qualitative shifts in the nature of the knowledge as a function of age.
